EXPERIMENT NO. 12
Object; TO DETERMINE THE RELATIVE SURFACE TENSION OF
UNKNOWN LIQUID BY DROP COUNT METHOD
APPARATUS REQUIRED
3. Beaker
1. Stalagmometer 2. Pyknometer
5. Clamp and stand
4. Rubber tube
CHEMICALS REQUIRED
1. Distilled water 2. Given liquid
THEORY

Molecules of surface liquid are only subjected to attractive force of molecules below these surface molecules so surface molecules are under tension. Surface tension can be defined as force per unit length acting perpendicular to the tangential line of the force. The spherical shape and the rise of liquid in capillary tube etc. are effect of surface tension. It depends upon temperature and density of liquid.

The relative surface tension of liquid can be determined in lab by drop count method. This method is based on counting number of drops of same volume of given liquid with respect to water using tube stalagmometer.

The formula used to calculate the relative surface tension of liquid is —IL nw dl nl x dw Where, YI = surface tension of given liquid yw = surface tension of water nl = number of drops of liquid nw = number of drops of water dl = density of liquid dw = density of water densities can be determined by measuring mass with help Of pyknometer. dl Mw
Miscellaneous where MI and Mw are the masses of same volume of liquid and water in pyknometer.

PROCEDURE
Take a stalagmometer and a pykometer, wash with chromic acid followed by water and dry them.
Take the weight of empty and dry pykometer. Fill it with given liquid and water in turn and note down weight again.
Ringe the stalagmometer with liquid and clamp it verücally in stand.
Take given liquid in a beaker and suck the liquid in the stalagmometer upon upper mark of tube with help of rubber tube.
Count the number of complete drops as the liquid passes from upper mark to lower mark and record it.
Repeat this process three times and carry out same process for distilled.

THEORY

Viscosity is defined as the internal resistance to the flow of liquid which one layer possess to another layer trying to pass over it. The liquid having high viscosity flow at slow rate and vice-versa.

Rate of flow of liquid is inversely proportional to Eme taken for flow so relaüve rate of flow of liquid is determined by finding out the time of flow of a given volume of liquid through a capillary of viscometer with respect to same volume of water.

Let rl and rw be the rate of flow of given liquid and water and tl and tw be time taken for flow. Then relative rate of flow of liquid with respect to water is, rl tl rw The coefficient of viscosity (n) is defined as the force in dyne per square centimefre required to maintain a difference of velocity of lcm/sec between two parallel layers of liquid held at a distance of 1 cm apart.
